Final-round prep for Lincoln International, analyst role. Plan first, then one question.
Timeline:
- 3 to 4 days out: re-read the posting and every interviewer's name you have. Write a one-page summary of why you want this firm and this analyst role, in your own words.
- 2 days out: prepare 3 stories with a number each (a project, a time you disagreed or pushed back, a time you missed something and fixed it). Each should run situation, what you did, result.
- 1 day out: practice out loud for 20 minutes. Record yourself if you can; listen for filler and for answers that run past two minutes.
- Day of: review your stories, your summary and two or three questions for them. Get there or log in 10 minutes early.
Topics to cover for a final round at an analyst level:
- Why this firm, and why this role specifically, not just finance or analytics in general.
- Your most relevant project or work, walked through with the numbers and your part in it.
- How you handle ambiguity, a deadline you can't fully meet, and feedback you disagree with.
- Technical or case questions for the role. Expect a live exercise or a market or company question; practice a structured answer out loud.
- Your questions for them: about the team's work, how analysts grow, what a strong first year looks like.
What to practice: the three stories out loud, a 60-second "walk me through your background," and one structured case answer timed at 10 minutes.
